statement: Let $f(x)=\dfrac{1}{x-1}$ for $x\neq1$. Show that $f(f(x))=f(x)-1$ is not generally true, but find $f(f(x))$ explicitly and solve $f(f(x))=x$.
solution: $f(f(x))=\dfrac{1}{\frac{1}{x-1}-1}=\dfrac{1}{\frac{1-(x-1)}{x-1}}=\dfrac{x-1}{2-x}$ for $x\neq2$. Setting $f(f(x))=x$ gives $\dfrac{x-1}{2-x}=x$, so $x-1=x(2-x)=2x-x^{2}$, i.e. $x^{2}-x-1=0$. Hence $x=\dfrac{1\pm\sqrt{5}}{2}$.
hints: Substitute f(x) into f and simplify the double fraction.
Set the result equal to x.
